candidates.summary: the frameless path sets m.Exception and go-panics without clearing it, so a reused Machine re-raises the old panic on later normal calls
candidates.failure_scenario: In `gno repl` (RunStatements recovers and keeps r.m): `a := ""`, then `b := a[0]` prints the right error but leaves r.m.Exception set. A later `func k() int { defer println("d"); return 4 }` then `println(k())` prints `d` and fails with `runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0` instead of printing 4, and the next unrelated panic (`z := 0`, `d := 1/z`) reports the old index error chained ahead of the division by zero. At the merge base the nil deref aborted before m.Exception was assigned, so the same session printed `d` then `4`. Keeper paths are unaffected: each Machine is Released per call and Release zeroes *m. The REPL was already broken after a function-level unhandled panic (doOpPanic2 path, different symptom at base and head), so the fix belongs where the REPL recovers: reset the machine's exception state there.

candidates.failure_scenario: `gno run main.gno` with `var a = ""; var A = a[0]` at head prints `panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0`, then `goroutine 1 [running]:` and a host stack into machine.go:3285, exit 2. m.RunFiles at run.go:299 has no recover, unlike runExpr below it, which turns an UnhandledPanicError into an error.
